plan.title: Rewrite README + top-level docs around init/update/doctor

narratives.Description: Rewrite the README and top-level docs (BROWNFIELD, UPGRADING) around the three-command model (init / update / doctor) now that the behavior in the epic's children has landed, routing users by situation to exactly one command. Getting Started leads with `npm i -g @deftai/directive` then `directive init`; brownfield docs start with `directive init` rather than submodule/clone/legacy-installer paths; UPGRADING points ordinary users to `directive update` while preserving advanced detail; and the README gitignore claim is reconciled with reality (ignore `.deft/core/`, `.deft/.cli/`, `ritual-state.json`, cache -- NOT `package.json`).
narratives.Overview:
Part of epic #2203. Absorbs #2201. Ships last, after behavior lands.

## Summary

Rewrite README and top-level docs around the three-command model (`init` / `update` / `doctor`), routing users by situation, after the behavior in #child A–I is real or staged behind the contract.

## Scope

- README "Getting Started" starts with `npm i -g @deftai/directive`, then `directive init`.
- Route by situation: new empty project -> `init`; existing codebase -> `init`; existing Directive project -> `update`; unsure/broken -> `doctor`; legacy/pre-v0.20 -> `init`/`doctor` routes to the specific migration path.
- BROWNFIELD docs start with `directive init`, not submodule/clone/legacy-installer paths.
- UPGRADING preserves advanced detail but points ordinary users to `directive update`.
- Reconcile the README gitignore claim with reality (ignore `.deft/core/`, `.deft/.cli/`, `ritual-state.json`, cache; NOT `package.json`).

## Acceptance criteria

- README/BROWNFIELD/UPGRADING and top-level help all agree on the three-command model.
- Gitignore claim matches actual `init`/`update` behavior.
- Docs do not promise location-independent `init` beyond what #child A delivers (matched vs mismatched scoped honestly).
- Snapshot tests for top-level help.

## Related

Absorbs #2201. Depends on #child A–I + #child J1. Parent #2203.
narratives.UserStory: As a new or returning Directive user deciding how to adopt or repair the framework, I want the README and BROWNFIELD and UPGRADING docs plus the top-level help to route me by situation through the single three-command init/update/doctor model with an honest gitignore claim, so that I always know which one command to run for my situation and the docs never promise behavior the tools do not deliver.
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
1. Rewrite the README `Getting Started` around the three-command model: lead with `npm i -g @deftai/directive` then `directive init`, and add a route-by-situation table (new empty -> init; existing codebase -> init; existing Directive project -> update; unsure/broken -> doctor; legacy/pre-v0.20 -> init/doctor routes to the specific migration path). Build on the cold-start block already added by #2273 rather than duplicating it.
2. Rewrite `content/docs/BROWNFIELD.md` to START with `directive init` (not submodule/clone/legacy-installer paths), and update `content/UPGRADING.md` to point ordinary users at `directive update` while preserving the advanced/big-jump detail.
3. Reconcile the README gitignore claim with reality: ignore `.deft/core/`, `.deft/.cli/`, `ritual-state.json`, and cache -- NOT `package.json`; fix the stale `scaffolds vbrief/` phrasing to the canonical `xbrief/` layout.
4. Scope `init` honesty: docs MUST NOT promise location-independent init beyond what the merged #2265 dispatcher delivers (matched vs mismatched described honestly). Ensure README/BROWNFIELD/UPGRADING and top-level help all agree on the three-command model.
5. Update/extend the content-contract standards tests (`packages/core/src/content-contracts/standards/readme_brownfield.test.ts`, `upgrading_sections.test.ts`) and the top-level help snapshot in `packages/cli/src/dispatch.test.ts` so the three-command agreement + gitignore claim are asserted. Add a brief CHANGELOG entry. Run `task ts:check-lane`, targeted vitest, and `task check:framework-source`.
